cards.title: The strip tells you more than Papa
cards.body: Parents rarely say they are confused about their medicines. They just quietly get it wrong. Here are five signs worth noticing on your next visit home.

cards.title: Strips that never seem to finish
cards.body: If last month's BP strip still looks nearly full, doses are probably being missed. Count gently. This is a check, not an interrogation.

cards.title: Or strips that finish too fast
cards.body: Running out early can mean extra doses taken by mistake. Worth a calm chat with the doctor or chemist, not a family meeting.

cards.title: Two boxes, same medicine
cards.body: A different brand from a different chemist can look like a brand new medicine. Duplicates in the drawer are a classic sign of mix-ups.

cards.title: "Haan, le li" with zero details
cards.body: Ask which one they took and when. If the answer is vague every single time, they may need a simpler system, not a lecture.

cards.title: New dizziness, drowsiness or falls
cards.body: These can have many causes, medicines included. Mention them to the doctor rather than guessing. Sudden confusion or weakness on one side needs urgent help: call 112.

cards.title: Notice, then help quietly
cards.body: None of this is about catching them out. Spot the pattern, make the routine easier, and keep their doctor in the loop.

takeaway: Unfinished strips, duplicate boxes and vague answers often mean a parent needs simpler medicine support, not a scolding.
share: Send this to whoever is visiting Mummy-Papa this weekend.
